clips.verdict: The moment is clean and usable, but the cut is too long and the clip never got distributed (0 views after 107h), so the data says nothing about the moment itself.
clips.worked: It's the only clip with no swearing problems. The premise (a fan read a whole seduction book to write a letter) is clear in one sentence. The payoff line, 'be yourself, everybody else is already taken', is quotable.

titles: Creator name first, then the setup, never the result. Speed, Jynxzi and Adin all gave away the payoff in the title ('Red Card', 'Copper', 'Hang On').
Sell the joke, not the trivia. 'Asks If This Dog Is Ever Sad' beats 'Japan's Most Popular Dog'. Plain verbs, 1-2 emoji at the end, and only claims the audio backs up.
hooks: Write the hook as the question or stake the clip answers within 15s ('IF PALMER SCORES, STREAM ENDS', 'GUESS HIS RANK FROM HIS NAME'), never a mood label.
The narrator states the promise and stops. Ban 'and then this happened' and any line that hints at the punchline. If the narrator line repeats the hook text, cut one of them.
clip_picks: Pick moments whose premise is one spoken line a cold viewer gets: a bet, a guess, a countdown, a question. Athlete or celebrity crossovers with Speed and Kai first. The Speed vs. Palmer clip is the only one that got any views.
Listen to the full clip before cutting. Two of these six clips (Kai/Ray and Adin) shipped with unmuted n-words. If a slur can't be muted without killing the payoff, skip the clip.
Skip moments that only work visually or depend on crosstalk (fans chasing Kai, breed talk). If the transcript doesn't make sense read out loud, a scroller won't get it either.
length_and_pacing: All six clips are exactly 53s, which looks like a template, not an edit. Cut each clip to its own length: start ≤2s before the stake line, end ≤2s after the payoff. Most of these come out at 18-30s.
Every clip has 15-25s of trailing banter after the payoff. Ending on the payoff line ('That's a wrap', 'already taken', 'GG's') is what drives loops.
Hand-fix burned-in captions on the key line whenever the speech is fast or slurred.
posting: Six clips at 0-15 views with n/a analytics across the board after 107-162h is a distribution problem, not just a clip problem. Fix that before judging any pick.
Post 1-2 clips a day, within hours of the stream, so you catch people searching for it. Clips from streams days old compete with hundreds of other clippers.
After 48h, judge each clip on 3s retention and share of views from the Shorts feed, and only once Studio actually shows those numbers.

money.why: Campaigns usually pay per view on clips you post, so they pay before YPP does, and N3on is the one creator here with a known campaign. The bet/countdown format that fits Speed also fits N3on's stream moments.
money.first_step: Find the current N3on campaign listing (his Discord or the clipping platform hosting it), read its rules on narration, length and slurs, and post 2 N3on clips that follow the stake-hook format within hours of a stream.

money.idea: Join other creators' official clipping programs on campaign platforms like Whop Content Rewards
money.why: Kai, Speed and similar creators sometimes run paid clip campaigns. Your edit style (pinned hook, short cut) is what those campaigns pay for, and you're already clipping these creators for free.
money.first_step: Search the campaign platforms for active campaigns from Kai Cenat, IShowSpeed, Jynxzi or Adin Ross, and only clip creators with a live campaign until the channel has traction.

money.idea: Weekly long-form recap ('This Week's Best Streamer Moments')
money.why: It reuses the same cuts, fits the channel name 'Late Recaps', and builds watch hours toward the long-form YPP path (1,000 subs + 4,000 hours). It also gives subscribers a reason to subscribe that Shorts alone don't.
money.first_step: Once at least 3 Shorts clear their first 48h with feed traffic, put the week's 8-10 best uncut moments into a single 8-12 min video with chapters, and link it from each Short's comments.

next_actions: Find out why nothing is being shown. In Studio, check every clip for copyright claims, age restrictions, a 'made for kids' setting and Shorts classification (vertical, under 3 min). Also check whether Studio shows any analytics at all. Then test one clean clip with no AI narrator, to rule out the narrator causing reused or inauthentic-content suppression.
Set the Adin/Osiris clip and the Kai/Ray clip to private today because of the unmuted slurs. Re-upload Kai/Ray only if the slur can be muted without losing 'stay behind me'.

From now on, post 1-2 clips a day within hours of a live stream, prioritizing Speed and Kai crossover moments, each cut to its own length (no fixed 53s template).
